title: Typed routes in Fastify
summary: Register a route with typed params and a response schema that shapes the payload.

scenario.briefing: The campus catalog is moving to Fastify for schema-based serialization. Expose one product with a typed route and a stable response shape.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Pass Params and Reply to app.get as type arguments.
Put the route path first and the options object second.
Declare both a 200 and a 404 response schema.
Use reply.status(404).send for the missing product.

misconceptions.description: Returning an error object without setting the status.
misconceptions.feedback: A returned object is serialized as 200. Set the status through reply when the resource is missing.
misconceptions.testDescription: A missing product answers 404 through the reply object.

misconceptions.description: Assuming TypeScript generics also validate the request.
misconceptions.feedback: Generics disappear at runtime. Add request schemas when untrusted input must be checked.
misconceptions.diagnostic: TypeScript generics are erased, so they do not validate params at runtime.

misconceptions.description: Believing Fastify infers params without a generic or schema.
misconceptions.feedback: Fastify does not infer route params from the path. Add the route generic or a params schema.

sections.title: The route generic types the request
sections.body: Fastify reads the generic on app.get to type Params, Body, Querystring, and Reply. Typing params keeps the handler aligned with the path it serves.

sections.title: Schemas do two jobs
sections.body: A request schema validates incoming data before the handler runs. A response schema serializes the reply, which also prevents accidental extra fields from leaving the service.

sections.title: Handlers can return or reply
sections.body: Returning a value lets Fastify serialize it through the response schema. Use reply when you need to set a status such as 404 before sending.

vocabulary.definition: The TypeScript type arguments that describe a route's request and reply shapes.

steps.title: Register a typed product route
steps.prompt: Edit server.ts. Create the Fastify instance, register GET /products/:id with typed params, and return the product or a 404 with the response schema.

tests.description: The instance is created and the typed route is registered.
includes: app.get<{ Params: { id: string }; Reply: Product | { error: string } }>

tests.description: The route declares params and response schemas.
The handler looks up the product by the typed param.
A missing product answers 404 through the reply object.

hints: Create the instance with Fastify({ logger: false }).
Register app.get<{ Params: { id: string }; Reply: Product | { error: string } }>("/products/:id", ...).
Add params and response schemas to the route options.
Use reply.status(404).send({ error: "not_found" }) when the product is missing.

steps.title: Typed routing

statements.label: The route generic describes params, body, query, and reply for the handler.
A response schema both documents and filters the serialized payload.
An async Fastify handler may return the payload instead of calling reply.send.
Fastify leaves params untyped unless the whole server is generated from a schema.

steps.explanation: Fastify uses route generics for compile-time types and JSON schemas for runtime validation and serialization. A 404 still needs a declared response shape so its body is consistent.
hints: Check each statement against Fastify's type and schema split.
Remember that generics are erased at runtime.
Confirm when a response schema filters fields.
Select statements about generics, schemas, and reply handling.
